ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The diagram above represents the idealized titration curve for the reaction of sodium oxalate ($Na_2C_2O_4$) with a strong acid like hydrochloric acid ($HCl$). E and F represent the pH at the endpoints. G and H will depend on the composition of the sample with the possibility that one may not be present. In addition to water, what are the predominant species in solution at E?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The graph is a titration curve with pH on the vertical axis and volume of strong acid added on the horizontal axis. As acid is added, the pH decreases in two main stages: a first steep drop associated with endpoint E, followed by a lower plateau, then a second steep drop associated with endpoint F. The horizontal positions G and H mark acid volumes corresponding to the two drops/endpoints. Reasoning: The titration is sodium oxalate, Na2C2O4, with strong acid HCl. Oxalate, C2O4^2−, is diprotic as a base and is protonated stepwise. At the first endpoint E, one equivalent of H+ has been added per oxalate ion, so the predominant oxalate-containing species is HC2O4−, not yet H2C2O4. Sodium ions from Na2C2O4 and chloride ions from HCl remain as spectator ions. Therefore, excluding water, the predominant species at E are Na+, Cl−, and HC2O4−.

From the text, the titration is sodium oxalate with strong acid HCl. At the first endpoint, exactly the first protonation of oxalate has been completed, so C2O4^2- has been converted predominantly to HC2O4^- but not yet to H2C2O4. Include spectator ions from the salts/acid, giving Na+, Cl-, and HC2O4^- as the predominant non-water species.

method.method_draft: First note from the diagram that E corresponds to the first endpoint reached as HCl is added. Set up the first-endpoint stoichiometric reaction: Na2C2O4 + HCl -> NaHC2O4 + NaCl. Then dissociate the soluble ionic compounds in water: NaHC2O4 supplies Na+ and HC2O4^-, and NaCl supplies Na+ and Cl-. Combining duplicate spectator sodium ions, the predominant species besides water are Na+, Cl-, and HC2O4^-.
